prompt: DUMMY model (not a real charge). Buy and sell Rs 5,000 of a stock at the same price. Proportional 0.1% per leg, Rs 20 fixed per order, Rs 50 DP charge on the sell. What is the total round-trip cost?
solution: Buy leg: 0.1% x 5,000 = 5; plus fixed 20; total 25. Sell leg: 0.1% x 5,000 = 5; plus fixed 20; plus DP 50; total 75. Round trip: 25 + 75 = 100.

prompt: Using the same DUMMY model and the Rs 5,000 round trip (total cost Rs 100), what is the break-even move as a percentage of the position value?
solution: Total cost / position value = 100 / 5,000 = 0.02 = 2.0%. This is approximate, because the exit price changes the proportional charges.

prompt: A broker shows zero brokerage on a delivery order. A trader concludes, "Zero brokerage means the trade is free." Is the conclusion right?

options.text: Yes, because brokerage is the only cost that applies
No, because other cost components can still apply, and brokerage is only one line in the list
Yes, if the trade is small enough
No, because zero brokerage is itself a sign of a fraud

explanations.a: Brokerage is one of several components. Exchange charges, the SEBI fee, stamp duty, GST and the DP charge on a sell can all apply, depending on the rules that must be verified.
explanations.c: Size changes how much each fixed charge weighs, but it does not remove the charges. A small trade is more expensive as a share of its value, not free.
explanations.d: Zero brokerage is not evidence of fraud. The point is that one line on a statement is never the whole cost.

prompt: Spot the mistake: "I found a brokerage rate on a finance blog, so I will use that rate in my cost plan." Which part of this is wrong?

options.text: It is fine if the blog post is recent
A rate must be checked against the official source, with the date of the check, before it is used
Blog rates are always correct once they are published
Only the broker's rates matter, so exchange and government rates can be ignored

explanations.a: Recency does not make a rate official. A recent blog post can still be wrong, out of date or about a different segment.
explanations.c: Being published does not make a rate correct. Rates change, and the official page is the only reliable source for them.
explanations.d: The cost plan has several components from different bodies. Ignoring the exchange, SEBI, state and government lines underestimates the cost.

prompt: In the DUMMY model used in this chapter, which charges apply to the SELL leg of a Rs 5,000 round trip? Select all that apply.

options.text: DP charge of Rs 50 on the sale
Nothing, because a sell carries no charges

explanations.d: A sell leg carries charges in the dummy model: the fixed per-order charge, the proportional charge and the DP charge on the sale. Only the buy leg has no DP charge.

prompt: Hypothetical. Two DUMMY round trips have the same percentage price move. Trade X is Rs 5,000 and trade Y is Rs 50,000. Using the DUMMY model, which trade has the higher cost as a percentage of its value?

options.text: Trade X, at 2.0% of its value
Trade Y, at 0.38% of its value
Both are the same, because the rates are the same
Trade Y, because it costs more rupees in total

explanations.b: 0.38% is the cost of trade Y, the larger trade. Trade X has the higher percentage because fixed charges are spread over less value.
explanations.c: The rates are the same, but the fixed charges do not scale with value, so the percentages differ.
explanations.d: Trade Y costs more rupees (Rs 190 against Rs 100), but a larger total does not mean a larger share of the position.
